svg.title: How the YouTube Toolkit commands fit together
svg.desc: The toolkit drawn as an editing timeline of one video. On the left, youtube search, natively or semantically with embeddings, and youtube channel find videos, and one is passed on. The youtube video command is a stack of tracks along the video's timeline, one per flag: metadata with its chapters and a sponsor span, comments, the transcript, and the download need no key, with speech-to-text standing in when a video has no captions, and the download saving the picture and its sound whole or as a bracketed range. Below a divider, refine and translate, the summary, and vision are switched on by a model: the first two by an LLM, vision by the screenshots install, with frames ranked by a decision model or else embeddings. A row at the bottom lists the five things that can be switched on: screenshots, speech-to-text, embeddings, a decision model, and an LLM. A playhead plays across the tracks from left to right, jumps over the sponsor span, and starts again.

g.text: TAKE WHAT YOU NEED FROM IT
each flag adds a part, all from one fetch of the video
FIVE THINGS YOU CAN SWITCH ON
youtube setup saves the keys, youtube doctor shows what is on
a key, or a local model
